llm.summary: The skill's stated promise of 100% local protection conflicts with other parts of its own documentation that describe cloud registration and per-call network classification — this mismatch and some ambiguous instructions warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a local, runtime security plugin that never sends data to OpenGuardrails, yet the reference doc describes agent registration, POST /api/v1/agents/register and per-call POST /api/v1/detect to openguardrails.com (Core). That is a direct contradiction: either detection is local or it is cloud-based. The requirement set in the registry (no env vars, no binaries) is consistent with an instruction-only plugin, but the documented network behavior (registration, detection, storing agent API keys) implies capabilities not declared in the registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions include installing the plugin via openclaw plugins install and running gateway restart (expected), testing by reading a sample file under ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard (expected sample), and explicit commands that reveal or request API keys and agent IDs (/og_status, /og_config, /og_claim). The SKILL.md also mandates relaying any <openguardrails-quota-exceeded> content 'in full' to the user, which could cause the agent to display whatever the cloud returns without restriction. Overall the instructions are specific but grant the plugin/agent authority to handle and display API keys and account info and to follow upgrade flows — behavior that should be explicit and transparent to the user.

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files in the registry — lowest install risk from registry perspective. The SKILL.md directs users to run openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard, which is reasonable for an OpenClaw plugin. There is no direct download URL or extract instruction in the registry itself.

dimensions.detail: The registry declares no required env vars or credentials, but the documentation repeatedly references Agent ID, API key, stored credentials at ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json, and actions that surface API keys (/og_status). That implies the plugin will manage/require an API key and persist it locally despite the registry not declaring any primaryEnv or required env variables. This mismatch between declared and implied credential handling is noteworthy.

dimensions.detail: always:false and agent-autonomy are normal. The docs state the plugin registers the agent, stores an API key locally, and shares quota across claimed agents — so it will persist credentials/config under the user's home directory and can be invoked by the agent. This is not automatically privileged, but combined with the cloud-classification behavior it increases blast radius if the network interactions are misrepresented.

llm.guidance: Before installing, verify the true dataflow and code provenance: 1) Inspect the upstream repository and package contents (npm pack --dry-run, tar extraction) and compare to the GitHub source as suggested in references/details.md. 2) Confirm whether detection is truly local or uses OpenGuardrails Core — the SKILL.md claims 100% local processing but the reference file describes POST /api/v1/detect to openguardrails.com; ask the maintainer to clarify. 3) If you test, run network monitoring (tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch) during registration/activation to confirm outbound destinations and payloads and ensure no sensitive data is sent. 4) Be cautious about entering or exposing API keys: the plugin appears to persist an Agent API key to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json and exposes it via /og_status — only use keys you control and are willing to revoke. 5) Consider trying the plugin in an isolated environment or ephemeral agent before enabling on production agents. 6) If you need higher assurance, request the exact package tarball + a pointer to the exact commit/tag in the GitHub repo and have someone you trust audit index.ts and platform-client network code for what metadata is sent. Install only after the above checks satisfy you or if the maintainer provides a clear, auditable statement that no non-sanitized secrets leave your machine.
